title: Code Injection in eval and Command Substitution
platform_conditions: POSIX sh and bash on Linux/macOS; BASH_ENV/ENV startup-file behavior is bash/sh-specific and does not apply to scripts run with the -p (privileged) setuid path
security_mechanism: eval concatenates its arguments and hands the string back through the full grammar a second time, so any quoting that survived the first parse is re-interpreted: a semicolon, pipe, backtick or $(...) inside the input becomes shell syntax, not text. The same re-parse happens in indirect expansion ${!var} (the named variable's own expansion is evaluated), in arithmetic contexts where $((expr)) expands variable names recursively, and in trap 'string' which is evaluated as code when the signal fires. Piping fetched content straight to an interpreter (curl ... | sh, eval "$(curl ...)") collapses transport integrity and execution into one step with no review point in between.

source_sink_clues.source: Text the script does not author: configuration values sourced from untrusted files, user replies from read, remote installer payloads fetched over the network, environment variables in a CI runner, or variable names supplied externally to ${!var} and declare.
source_sink_clues.sink: eval of dynamic strings; sh -c "$x"; source/. of externally chosen paths; ${!var} with an externally influenced name; arithmetic evaluation of input-derived expressions; trap "...$var..."; curl|sh and eval "$(curl ...)" pipelines

tracking_guards: Check the executed string is built from server-side constants only; check dynamic dispatch is replaced by a case allowlist instead of eval or ${!var}; check fetched content is written to a file, integrity-verified (checksum/signature), read, and only then executed; check trap bodies contain no variable interpolation; check arithmetic uses a validated numeric variable, not raw input text.
not_candidate_when: eval executes only literal constant strings (e.g. eval "$setflags" where setflags is defined verbatim in the script), the indirect name comes from a fixed internal set validated against ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$, or the fetched payload is pinned by a cryptographic checksum verified before execution with no network path around the check.
public_references: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command — https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
Bash Reference Manual: Bash Startup Files — https://www.gnu.org/software/bash/manual/html_node/Bash-Startup-Files.html
